subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
stem: The rate constants of a reaction at 500K and 700K are \(0.02\,\text{s}^{-1}\) and \(0.07\,\text{s}^{-1}\) respectively. Calculate the values of \(E_a\) and \(A\).
_note: Transcribed exactly as printed on p-20; three defects in the book's own printed solution. (1) The last step prints A = 0.02/0.012 = 1.61, but that division evaluates to 1.67. The book displays the exponential rounded to 0.012 while dividing by the unrounded value e^(-4.386) = 0.01243, which does give 1.61 — so the stated answer is right and the displayed arithmetic does not reproduce it. (2) E_a is printed as 18230.8 J with the per-mole dropped; it should be J mol^-1, since R was used as J K^-1 mol^-1. (3) A is printed without units; for a first-order reaction it carries s^-1. The R units in THIS example are printed correctly as J K^-1 mol^-1 (unlike Eg 3.10 — see its note).

subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
stem:
The first order rate constant for the decomposition of ethyl iodide by the reaction

\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I(g)} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{(g)} + \text{HI(g)}\)

at 600K is \(1.60 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{s}^{-1}\). Its energy of activation is \(209\,\text{kJ/mol}\). Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at 700K.
_note: The stem is on p-20 and the solution finishes on p-21 (band boundary); both halves are transcribed here. PRINTED-UNIT FAULT in the substitution line on p-21, confirmed at 3x magnification: the book prints the numerator as '209000 J mol L^-1' and the denominator as '2.303 x 8.314 J mol L^-1 K^-1' — a stray litre where the superscript -1 on 'mol' belongs. As printed those units are chemically impossible (R is J mol^-1 K^-1). Per the chemistry brief's rendered-glyph-fault rule the INTENDED units are transcribed (J mol^-1 and J mol^-1 K^-1) rather than the printed ones, so the stored solution does not teach a wrong unit for R. The same book prints the units correctly in Eg 3.9 one page earlier.

subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
stem:
The activation energy for the reaction

\(2\,\text{HI(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2 + \text{I}_2\text{(g)}\)

is \(209.5\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) at 581K. Calculate the fraction of molecules of reactants having energy equal to or greater than activation energy?
_note: Faithful to the page: the book prints the state symbol only on I_2, leaving H_2 without one (it is a gas). Transcribed as printed; the omission does not affect the chemistry or the answer.
